summary: Guided stepwise deactivation and safety-net for optimizer changes (batching / cache / quant profiles)
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Health reported a 3x tail latency increase and elevated 5xx rate after we applied an optimizer bundle (quant profile + aggressive batching + prefix caching changes) to their Dedicated pool in us-east. They requested guided rollback steps that preserve traffic while avoiding cold-start spikes and token-cost regressions.

Impact:
- ~15% of their live user requests saw end-to-end latency >2s (baseline ~600ms).
- Observed application-level 5xx errors (upstream timeouts) for streaming endpoints.
- Customer cannot pause traffic due to SLA requirements and needs a safe, staged deactivation.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity: d-pool-nimbus-us-east
- Serving runtime: rwd-serve v3.7.2 (custom build)
- Optimizer bundle: quant-profile: qprofile-alpha-2026-03, batching-window: 50ms -> 10ms, kv-cache-priority: enabled (prefetch on cold start)
- Affected model: gptx-13b-quant-v2 pinned by customer

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Customer triggers a traffic shift (canary) to new optimizer profile via Console rollout.
2) After ~10 minutes, streaming latencies increase and a subset of requests fail with 502 upstream timeouts.
3) Attempts to revert to previous profile from console caused transient spike in 5xx (~7 minutes) due to GPUs returning cold and increased per-token cost.

Logs / metrics pointers:
- Dashboard: Console -> d-pool-nimbus-us-east -> p50/p95/p99, request errors.
- Trace sample: trace-id 7f3a2c (attached in Slack thread #support-nimbus).
- Metrics link: https://metrics.redwood.ai/dashboards/nimbus-optimizer-regressions

Requested outcome:
- A step-by-step rollback that avoids cold-start amplification and avoids causing cost spike or double-serving.
- A short-term mitigation to immediately reduce 5xx and tail latency while longer-term postmortem is produced.

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Primary contributors to regression: 1) batching-window reduced aggressively from 50ms to 10ms leading to micro-batch growth and head-of-line queuing in the streaming connector; 2) quant profile qprofile-alpha-2026-03 introduced a changed memory layout causing higher KV cache invalidations; 3) autoscaler reacted to perceived pressure by evicting warm GPUs during transient error spikes which exacerbated cold-starts on revert.
Evidence collected:
- KV cache miss rate jumped from 2% -> 18% after bundle applied (metrics link).
- Queue depth histograms align with increased micro-batches.
- Traces show time spent waiting in runtime dispatch queue increased by ~120ms per request.
Hypotheses tested during live session:
- Reverting quant profile alone would not immediately improve latencies due to warmed vs cold GPU mismatch.
- Incrementally raising batching window to intermediate value reduced queue head pressure.
- Disabling prefetch removed spurious cache invalidation storms.
Actions taken:
- Performed intermediate rollback: batching 10ms -> 25ms; kv-cache prefetch off; set runtime flag deopt-guard-mode=true.
- Pre-warmed GPU pool with 5% shadow traffic for 12 minutes to refill KV caches before broader traffic shift.
- Monitored p99/p95 and 5xx for 30 minutes before proceeding to broader rollout.
Open follow-ups:
- Add a safety-check in Console to prevent applying optimizer bundles without a canary and pre-warm steps for Dedicated pools.
- Improve autoscaler heuristics to avoid evicting warm GPUs during transient error spikes.
- Re-evaluate qprofile-alpha on canary instances for KV invalidation patterns.
resolution:
Short-term resolution applied on 2026-03-11: executed staged deactivation sequence with customer on call. Resulted in p95 improvement ~30% and 5xx rate returned to baseline.

Detailed rollback steps performed (for audit / reproducibility):
1) Create new optimizer variant tag 'nimbus-safe-rollback-2026-03-11' which keeps quant-profile but sets batching-window=25ms and kv-cache-prefetch=false.
2) Use route-by-tag to shift 5% of traffic to the safe variant and monitor metrics for 10 minutes.
3) If stable, increase to 25% for additional 10 minutes, then 50%. During each step keep shadow traffic (5%) routed to previous profile to warm caches.
4) Once 50% stable for 15 minutes, coordinate with customer to move remaining traffic. If any step shows p95 degrade >15% or 5xx increase >3x baseline, roll back immediately to previous stable tag and notify SRE.
5) Post-change: run warmup job for 12 minutes to rebuild KV caches, then scale down warm pool to normal target.

Long-term actions scheduled:
- (ENG-PR-2394) Add Console guardrail: require canary + pre-warm toggle for optimizer bundles on Dedicated.
- (SRE-2389) Adjust autoscaler cooldown and eviction policy to avoid warm GPU eviction on transient spikes.
- (RESEARCH-514) Run offline analysis for qprofile-alpha and update quant pipelines to maintain KV layout stability.

Customer confirmation: Nimbus Health validated stabilization on 2026-03-12 and requested the playbook be added to their support onboarding. Ticket to remain open until follow-ups are complete.
